subject: Security request funnel: audit export, retention carveouts, and KMS options
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@novaprospects.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.k@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaprospects.com
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: audit export & BYOK handoff for pilot

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking our inbound request. We're starting a small pilot to evaluate Redwood for a regulated workflow and have three asks we'd like to triage:

1) Audit log export frequency and schema: we need transaction-level audit logs (user id, request id, model, prompt hash, timestamps) exported daily to our S3 with HMAC.
2) Retention carveout for a subset of records: some records need 13 months retention, others can be 30 days.
3) BYOK/KMS integration: we want to bring our key material and have a documented handoff process; escrow options are a concern for legal.

I attached our compliance questionnaire (nova_compliance_questionnaire_v2.pdf). Please point us to the minimal gating checklist and next steps so we can plan procurement.

Appreciate a short list of what Redwood requires (evidence, configuration, lead times) so we can raise internally.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Senior InfoSec Manager
NovaProspects

--

Subject: Re: Request: audit export & BYOK handoff for pilot

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. I've skimmed the attachment and put initial owners on this thread. High level: we can support all three asks but there are decision points that change implementation effort and lead time.

Immediate next steps (owner in parens):
- Confirm retention buckets and sample volumes (Nova) — affects storage & export cadence.
- Decide whether the BYOK requirement is customer-managed KMS (customer HSM) or a limited-key escrow model (Nova + Legal) — impacts timeline and legal work (Ben).
- Technical intake: we need your S3 export endpoint, SSH fingerprint for ingestion, expected daily log volume and whether logs must be redacted at source (Irene).

Irene, Ben, Naomi — can each confirm their blocking questions below so we can provide a single checklist back to Alice? If this looks reasonable I'll schedule a 30-min triage call today or tomorrow.

I'll also open an internal JIRA (SEC-482) and link to the questionnaire.

Thanks,

From: irene_choi <irene.c@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.k@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@novaprospects.com>, ben_carter <ben.c@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: audit export & BYOK handoff for pilot

Markus / Alice — technical triage notes below. Short answers first: daily export ✅, retention buckets ✅, BYOK plausible but needs escrow/legal alignment and Dedicated routing for strongest isolation.

Details:
- Audit log schema: we can include requestId, userId, modelId, promptHash, responseHash, startTs, endTs, podId, routeVersion. If Nova needs raw prompts in the log (PII-sensitive), we must discuss in-line redaction or a secure export pipeline.
- Export mechanics: we support push-to-s3 with a server-side encryption header. For HMAC verification, we can sign manifests using a dealer key. We'll need the S3 prefix and an AWS IAM principal we can assume (or a pre-signed PUT flow).
- Retention carveouts: simplest path is tagging at ingest and applying TTL buckets in our export pipeline; cost/effort scales with cardinality of tags. If there are per-tenant overrides, that's more work.
- BYOK/KMS: options ranked by isolation/cost: (1) Hosted: customer-provided CMK in their cloud account (preferred); (2) Dedicated: Redwood-managed VM with customer key material injected for session; (3) Escrow: limited use key signing for audit manifests (legal-heavy). If Nova requires HSM-backed keys we need to validate vendor and interop.

Blocking questions for Nova:
- Will you provide an IAM role or do we need to presign uploads?
- Which exact retention classes map to which S3 prefix?
- Do you require prompt text in logs or only hashed identifiers?

Workarounds: if BYOK can't be in place for the pilot, we can offer a 'semi-isolated' Dedicated pool with encrypted-at-rest keys managed by Redwood but strict export and access controls for Nova's ops team. That reduces legal friction but is not full BYOK.

I'll attach a quick note with technical options.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Infrastructure Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.c@redwood.com

From: ben_carter <ben.c@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-30T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: audit export & BYOK handoff for pilot

Looping legal/procurement context here — quick commercial proposal to keep the pilot moving:

- Route pilot to a small Dedicated tenancy with reserved capacity (2-4 GPUs). That gets us isolation guarantees and simplifies bringing customer keys for the session.
- Offer a 90-day retention window and a mapped export path for the 13-month carveout records (we can snapshot + transfer to Nova S3).
- Prepare a limited scope addendum for BYOK that states: pilot will use customer-provided CMKs where possible; if HSM escrow is required, we'll include an explicit escrow process and timeline (TBD).

If Markus/Irene sign off on the technical plan above, I can coordinate a short commercial term addendum and book a call for Tuesday 10am PT with Nova's procurement and our legal lead.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions & Compliance | Redwood Inference
ben.c@redwood.com
